chunks: He who does good does so for himself; and he who does evil suffers the consequence thereof. You have then to go back to your Lord.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between individual deeds and returning to God in the Quran?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited in Shia jurisprudence to establish the principle of individual responsibility (mas'uliyyah), clarifies that while the immediate consequences of actions are self-directed, the ultimate accountability lies with Allah. It underscores the dual nature of human agency, where one's deeds are an extension of the self, yet the final return (ruju') is to the Creator for divine reckoning.
